artifact.self_contained_problem:
An equation $f(x_1,\dots,x_n)=0$ in positive integers is called partition regular if, for every finite coloring $\mathbb{N}=C_1\cup C_2\cup\cdots\cup C_r$ of the positive integers into finitely many classes, there exist some class $C_i$ and positive integers $x_1,\dots,x_n\in C_i$ (not all equal) satisfying $f(x_1,\dots,x_n)=0$.

Determine whether the Pythagorean equation
$$x^2+y^2=z^2$$
is partition regular. That is, decide whether for every finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ there must exist a monochromatic triple $(x,y,z)$ of positive integers with $x^2+y^2=z^2$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open in general. Heule, Kullmann, and Marek (2016) settled the case of 2-colorings via SAT computation (Boolean Pythagorean Triples), and recent work (Frantzikinakis–Klurman–Moreira and others, 2023–2024) established partition regularity for Pythagorean pairs and related partial results, but the full question for arbitrary finite colorings of x²+y²=z² is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Partition regularity of Pythagorean pairs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work shows that Pythagorean pairs are partition regular; the full triples problem remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: pairs version solved, full Pythagorean triples problem still open.

status_evidence.title: Solving and Verifying the Boolean Pythagorean Triples Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Heule, Kullmann, Marek confirmed the 2-coloring case via SAT.
status_evidence.claim: 2-coloring case resolved, general partition regularity still open.

status_evidence.title: Partition regularity of homogeneous quadratics: Current trends and challenges
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describes the Pythagorean partition regularity question as a central open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is still open as of recent surveys.
